device.model: scanning SQUID susceptometer microscope (Attocube ANC300 positioner)
device.name: Scanning SQUID microscope: Attocube coarse positioning (scanning-squid)

facts.text: A physical scanning SQUID microscope is represented by a Microscope or a subclass such as SusceptometerMicroscope, a QCoDeS Station of instrument components
SusceptometerMicroscope is the Microscope subclass for a scanning SQUID susceptometer and takes the configuration file and the temperature mode

The Microscope constructor closes every QCoDeS instrument, loads the configuration, starts file logging and adds the Attocube controller, the Lakeshore 372 and 331, the scanner, the SQUID and the lock-ins
The Attocube component is an ANC300 built from the configuration's atto entry
Importing the microscope module writes squid_units.txt into the current directory
approach steps the z Attocube by attosteps between capacitive touchdowns until a touchdown or a safety check breaks the loop
The ANC300 axis mode parameter reads with getm n and writes with setm n; its values are gnd, inp, cap, stp, off, stp+ and stp-
The axis voltage parameter is limited to the configured voltage limit of the temperature mode
ask_raw clears the device, sends the command twice, raises if the second reply contains ERROR and sleeps 0.2 s
stop(axis) writes 'stop n' and then sets the axis mode to gnd

step(axis, steps) refuses a non-integer, sets mode stp, sends stepu or stepd with the axis and the step count, writes stepw, sleeps abs(steps)/frequency*1.25 s, sets mode gnd and records the move in its metadata
step sends its stepu or stepd command with ask, not write
_parse_axis accepts an axis label or controller index of the configured axes
Initialising the ANC300 sets each axis frequency and voltage to the configured values, grounds each axis and prints the controller version
The Scanner constructor moves the scanner to [0, 0, 0]
get_pos reads the x, y and z scanner voltages with an NI-DAQ analog-input task and clamps each to the configured voltage limits
goto writes a ramp to an analog-output task created inside the call and waits until it is done
The documentation calls the approach the most dangerous part of a measurement: a missed touchdown crashes the SQUID into the sample using the Attocubes
The example configuration maps the Attocube axes x, y and z to controller axes 1, 2 and 3

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: no source bounds a number of Attocube steps, and the upstream writes each step command twice (atto.py:109-124, 169), so the steps one command makes are not known from the source: measure them on the bench first. How far a model may step each axis, and in which direction z approaches the sample, depend on the mounting and the sample (the documentation warns of crashing the SQUID into the sample with the Attocubes, docs/pages/workflow.rst:34-38, 54)

safe_state.description: every Attocube axis stopped and grounded: stop(axis) sends 'stop n' and sets mode gnd (atto.py:143-152) for z, x and y, and the e-stop succeeds only when each axis mode reads back gnd (getm, atto.py:71-79); the piezo scanner is not stopped (its ramps cannot be) and keeps its voltage
